title: Adjectives
text:
The best way to think about how adjectives work in Spanish is that the form (gender and plurality) of an adjective *needs to match up to the noun it's modifying or describing*.

For example:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
|  **el niño *pequeño***  | the small boy |
|  **la niña *pequeña***  | the small girl |
|  **los niños *pequeños***  | the small boys |
|  **las niñas *pequeñas***  | the small girls |

Adjectives that end in "-e" have a singular and plural form to match the nouns they modify (just add an "s" to create the plural), but they don't take different forms for gender.

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
|  **un hombre *inteligente***  | an intelligent man |
|  **una mujer *inteligente***  | an intelligent woman |
|  **los hombres *inteligentes***  | the intelligent men |
|  **las mujeres *inteligentes***  | the intelligent women |

Adjectives that end in consonants behave largely the same as those that end in "-e." They have a singular and plural form but don't change for grammatical gender. Just add "-es" to create the plural.

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
|  **un trabajo difícil**  | a difficult job |
|  **una clase difícil**  | a difficult class |
|  **los juegos difíciles**  | the difficult games |
|  **las preguntas difíciles**  | the difficult questions |

The only exception is when the adjective ends in a "z", in which case the "z" changes to "c" before adding "-es." For example, **feliz** (*happy*) becomes **felices**.

**Nationality**

Adjectives that describe a person's nationality and end in "-o" (mexicano, americano, italiano, etc.) behave just like other "-o" adjectives, with forms for both gender and quantity:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
|  **un hombre mexicano**  | a Mexican man |
|  **una mujer mexicana**  | a Mexican woman |
|  **los niños mexicanos**  | the Mexican children/boys |
|  **las niñas mexicanas**  | the Mexican girls |

Adjectives for nationality end in consonants (español, francés, japonés) do not have the same rules as other adjectives ending in consonants. These nationality adjectives *do* have feminine forms to match up to feminine nouns.

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
|  **un hombre español**  | a Spanish man |
|  **una mujer española**  | a Spanish woman |
|  **los niños españoles**  | the Spanish children/boys |
|  **las niñas españolas**  | the Spanish girls |

**Adjectives before the noun**

Adjectives that have to do with **quantity** (including numbers) most often appear *before* the noun they're modifying.

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
|  **muchos libros**  | many books |
|  **mucha comida**  | a lot of food |
|  **pocos carros**  | few cars |
|  **unas sillas**  | some chairs |
|  **cinco minutos**  | five minutes |

Bueno (*good*) and malo (*bad*) can both appear before nouns, which you'll see often. In this case, they drop the "-o" at the end of the word.

- libro bueno -> **buen libro**
- comida buena -> **buena comida**
- libro malo -> **mal libro**
- comida mala -> **mala comida**

**Grande** (*big, large*) behaves a little differently when it comes before a noun. When it's *after* a noun, it means big, but *before* a noun, it changes to **gran** (if singular) and means *great.*

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
|  **un perro grande**  | a big dog |
|  **un gran perro**  | a great dog |
|  **un gran presidente**  | a great president |

If we're talking about the *best* or *worst* of a noun, then the adjective usually comes ahead of it.

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
|  **el mejor estudiante**  | the best leader |
|  **la peor comida**  | the worst food |
|  **la menor cantidad**  | the least quantity |

title: Adverbs
text:
You can use adverbs in two ways: 

1. Add **-mente** to the end of feminine singular adjectives:

rápida -> **rápidamente**
*quick* -> *quickly*

lenta -> **lentamente**
*slow* -> *slowly*

facil -> **facilmente**
*easy* -> *easily*

2. Use the preposition **con** before the singular form of the noun:

pacientemente -> **con paciencia**
*patiently*

respetuosamente -> **con respeto**
*respectfully*

inteligentemente -> **con inteligencia**
*intelligently*

title: Commands
text:
In English, we use the third-person present form of a verb to issue a command (**run** there, **eat** this, **give** it to me, etc.), and we do the exact same in Spanish.

So, you use the same verb conjugation you would use when talking about **él** or **ella** to tell someone to do something:

**Toma la foto.**
*Take the photo.*

**Come la comida.**
*Eat the food.*

To tell someone *not* to do something, we switch to the second-person subjunctive, using the **tú** conjugation.

---

Here are a few examples:

**No tomes la foto.**
*Don't take the photo.*

**No comas la comida.**
*Do not eat the food.*

title: Conditional tense
text:
In the most basic terms, you can think of the Spanish conditional tense as very similar to using "would" in English.

To conjugate the conditional tense we add the corresponding endings to the *infinitive* form of the verb. In other words, no need to drop the -ar, -er, or -ir.

All three verb groups use the same endings:

|  **Pronoun**  |  **Ending**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | -ía |
| **tú** | -ías |
| **él/ella** | -ía | 
| **nosotros/nosotras** | -íamos |
| **ellos/ellas** | -ían |

Example:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **estudiar**  | to study |
| **(yo) estudiaría** | I would study |
| **(tú) estudiarías** | you would study |
| **(él/ella) estudiaría** | he/she would study | 
| **(nosotros) estudiaríamos** | we would study |
| **(ellos) estudiarían** | they would study |

title: Estar
text:
The verb **estar** means "to be" and is used for one's *current condition, location, and actions in progress.*

Estar is an irregular verb. Here are the present tense conjugations: 

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **estar**  | to be |
| (yo) **estoy** | I am |
| (tú) **estás** | you are |
| (él/ella) **está** | he/she is | 
| (nosotros) **estamos** | we are |
| (ellos) **están** | they are |

And the progressive tense, used for ongoing actions:

|  **Verb Type**  |  **New Ending**  |  **Example**  | 
| --------- | -------- | -------- |
| -ar  | **-ando** | hablando |
| -er  | **-iendo** | comiendo |
| -ir  | **-iendo** | escribiendo |

A few examples:

**Estamos en la casa.**  
*We're in the house.*

**Ella está cansada.**  
*She is tired.*

**Él está enfermo.**  
*He is sick.*

**Estoy escribiendo un libro.**  
*I'm writing a book.*

title: Future tense
text:
Spanish has two future tenses. The first is the **informal future**, so-called because it actually uses the present tense of the verb **ir** (*to go*), combined with another verb.

For example:

**Ella va a correr.**
*She is going to run.*

**Voy a cocinar mañana.**
*I'm going to cook tomorrow.*

In case you need to brush up on the conjugations for **ir**, here they are in this context:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **ir**  | to go |
| **(yo) voy a comer** | I am going to eat |
| **(tú) vas a comer** | you are going to eat |
| **(él/ella) va a comer** | he/she is going to eat | 
| **(nosotros) vamos a comer** | we are going to eat |
| **(ellos) van a comer** | they are going to eat |

The second future tense is called the **simple future**. Unlike the present and past tense, we simply add these endings to the end of the *infinitive form* of the verb. These endings apply to all three regular verb groups.

|  **Pronoun**  |  **Ending**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | -é |
| **tú** | -ás |
| **él/ella** | -á | 
| **nosotros/nosotras** | -emos |
| **ellos/ellas** | -án |

Example:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **estudiar**  | to study |
| **(yo) estudiaré** | I will study |
| **(tú) estudiarás** | you will study |
| **(él/ella) estudiará** | he/she will study | 
| **(nosotros) estudiaremos** | we will study |
| **(ellos) estudiarán** | they will study |

title: Greetings
text:
Example conversation:

**¡Hola! ¿Cómo estás?**
*Hello! How are you?*

**Bien, ¿y tú?**
*I'm well, and you?*

**Muy bien. ¿Cómo te llamas?**
*I'm very well. What's your name?*

**Me llamo ____.**
*My name's ____.*

**Mucho gusto. Yo soy ____.**
*Nice to meet you. I'm ____.*

**¿De dónde eres?**
*Where are you from?*

**Soy de México. ¿Y tú?**
*I'm from Mexico. And you?*

**Soy de los Estados Unidos. Vivo en Nueva York.**
*I'm from the United States. I live in New York.*

Key phrases:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **hola**  | hello |
| **adiós**  | goodbye |
| **hasta pronto**  | see you soon *(lit: until soon)* |
| **hasta luego**  | see you later *(lit: until later)* |
| **nos vemos**  | see you later *(lit: we'll see each other)* |
| **buenos días**  | good morning |
| **buenas tardes**  | good afternoon |
| **buenas noches**  | good evening, good night |

title: Imperfect past tense
text:
The **imperfect** is used for actions that occurred in the past but are either:
1. not seen as being completed or finished, and/or
2. do not have a definite beginning and end.

These include things you used to do, past dates and times, and talking about your age in the past.

**-ar verbs**

|  **Pronoun**  |  **Ending**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | -aba |
| **tú** | -abas |
| **él/ella** | -aba | 
| **nosotros/nosotras** | -abamos |
| **ellos/ellas** | -aban |

Example:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **hablar**  | to speak |
| **(yo) hablaba** | I spoke |
| **(tú) hablabas** | you spoke |
| **(él/ella) hablaba** | he/she spoke | 
| **(nosotros) hablabamos** | we spoke |
| **(ellos) hablaban** | they spoke |

**-er and -ir verbs**

|  **Pronoun**  |  **Ending**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | -ía |
| **tú** | -ías |
| **él/ella** | -ía | 
| **nosotros/nosotras** | -íamos |
| **ellos/ellas** | -ían |

Examples:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **comer**  | to eat |
| **(yo) comía** | I ate |
| **(tú) comías** | you ate |
| **(él/ella) comía** | he/she ate | 
| **(nosotros) comíamos** | we ate |
| **(ellos) comían** | they ate |

title: Irregular verbs estar
text:
**Querer**

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **querer**  | to want |
| **(yo) quiero** | I want |
| **(tú) quieres** | you want |
| **(él/ella) quiere** | he/she wants | 
| **(nosotros) queremos** | we want |
| **(ellos) quieren** | they want |

**Hacer**

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **hacer**  | to do |

| **(tú) haces** | you do |
| **(él/ella) hace** | he/she does | 
| **(nosotros) hacemos** | we do |
| **(ellos) hacen** | they do |

*Note: hacer can also mean "to make"*

**Decir**

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **decir**  | to say |
| **(yo) digo** | I say |
| **(tú) dices** | you say |
| **(él/ella) dice** | he/she says | 
| **(nosotros) decimos** | we say |
| **(ellos) dicen** | they say |

**Ir**

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **ir**  | to go |
| **(yo) voy** | I go |
| **(tú) vas** | you go |
| **(él/ella) va** | he/she goes | 
| **(nosotros) vamos** | we go |
| **(ellos) van** | they go |

**Venir**

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **venir**  | to come |
| **(yo) vengo** | I come |
| **(tú) vienes** | you come |
| **(él/ella) viene** | he/she comes | 
| **(nosotros) venimos** | we come |
| **(ellos) vienen** | they come |

**Saber**

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **saber**  | to know |
| **(yo) sé** | I know |
| **(tú) sabes** | you know |
| **(él/ella) sabe** | he/she knows | 
| **(nosotros) sabemos** | we know |
| **(ellos) saben** | they know |

*Note that there's an accent over the "e" in the first person conjugation (sé)*

title: Jump start
text:
There are many words we use in English that can be translated into Spanish with very few changes.

**-or words**

- el doctor
- el color
- el error
- un tractor

**-al words**

- animal
- criminal
- personal
- social

**-ble words**

- imposible
- flexible
- horrible
- inevitable

**-ic words**

Add -o to the end of the word.

- Atlántico
- público
- romántico
- democrático

*Note: the accent on these words marks where the emphasis is placed*

**-ent and -ant words**

Add -e to the end of the word.

- presidente
- accidente
- elefante
- inteligente
- excelente

**-ist words**

Add -a to the end of the word.

- novelista
- artista
- dentista
- idealista

**-ous words**

Switch out the “-ous” for “-oso.”

- famoso
- curioso
- ambicioso
- delicioso

**Spelling differences**

**“Ph” becomes “f”**

- alphabet -> **alfabeto**
- elephant -> **elefante**

**“Th” becomes “t”**

- author -> **autor**
- Catholic -> **Católico**

**“tion” becomes “ción”**

English words switch out their “tion” for a “ción” when switching to Spanish.

**Only double “l” and “r”**

The only letters that are ever doubled in Spanish are “l” and “r.” A double “l” makes a “y” sound (*pollo* sounds like “poyo”).

In the case where an English word has two of the same letter next to each other, that doubled letter just becomes a single one in Spanish.

- annual -> **anual**
- different -> **diferente**

title: Past participle perfect tenses
text:
To conjugate the past participle in Spanish, we remove the infinitive ending (-ar, -er, or -ir) and add **-ado** to -ar verbs, or **-ido** to -er and -ir verbs.

For example:

**cerrar** -> **cerrado**
*to close* -> *closed*

**construir** -> **construido**
*to build* -> *built*

Alone, a past participle can be used as an adjective. For example: 

**El restaurante está cerrado.**
*The restaurant is closed.*

**El juguete perdido**
*The lost toy*

**Passive voice**

We can also use the verb **ser** + *past participle* to express something in the passive voice.

**Las palabras son entendidas.**
*The words are understood.*

**La comida fue descubierto.**
*The food was discovered.*

If you'd like to talk about who performed an action using the passive voice, add in the word **por**, which, in this case, means "by."

**El libro fue escrito por el autor.**
*The book was written by the author.*

**La tarea es realizada por el estudiante.**
*The homework is done by the student.*

title: Past tense
text:
**Preterite**

The **preterite** is used for actions that are completed, that have a definite beginning and end.

**-ar verbs**

|  **Pronoun**  |  **Ending**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | -é |
| **tú** | -aste |
| **él/ella** | -ó | 
| **nosotros/nosotras** | -amos |
| **ellos/ellas** | -aron |

Examples:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **hablar**  | to speak |
| **(yo) hablé** | I spoke |
| **(tú) hablaste** | you spoke |
| **(él/ella) habló** | he/she spoke | 
| **(nosotros) hablamos** | we spoke |
| **(ellos) hablaron** | they spoke |

**-er and -ir verbs**

Fortunately for us, the -er and -ir verb endings are the same for the preterite.

|  **Pronoun**  |  **Ending**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | -í |
| **tú** | -iste |
| **él/ella** | -ió | 
| **nosotros/nosotras** | -imos |
| **ellos/ellas** | -ieron |

Example of an -er verb:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **comer**  | to eat |
| **(yo) comí** | I ate |
| **(tú) comiste** | you ate |
| **(él/ella) comió** | he/she ate | 
| **(nosotros) comimos** | we ate |
| **(ellos) comieron** | they ate |

Example of an -ir verb:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **vivir**  | to live |
| **(yo) viví** | I lived |
| **(tú) viviste** | you lived |
| **(él/ella) vivió** | he/she lived | 
| **(nosotros) vivimos** | we lived |
| **(ellos) vivieron** | they lived |

title: Perfect tenses
text:
We can combine the verb **haber** (*to have*) with the past participle to create the perfect tenses.

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **haber**  | to have |
| **(yo) he** | I have |
| **(tú) has** | you have |
| **(él/ella) ha** | he/she has | 
| **(nosotros) hemos** | we have |
| **(ellos) han** | they have |

A few examples:

**He comido** los dulces.
*I **have eaten** the candy.*

El estudiante **ha estudiado** para el examen.
*The student **has studied** for the test.*

Los niños **han jugado** ese juego.
*The kids **have played** that game.*

title: Present tense
text:
Spanish verbs change form to indicate not only the tense and state of an action, but also *who is performing the action.*

**-ar verb conjugation**

|  **Pronoun**  |  **Ending**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | -o |
| **tú** | -as |
| **él/ella** | -a | 
| **nosotros/nosotras** | -amos |
| **ellos/ellas** | -an |
| **ustedes** | -an |

Examples:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **hablar**  | to speak |
| **(yo) hablo** | I speak |
| **(tú) hablas** | you speak |
| **(él/ella) habla** | he/she speaks | 
| **(nosotros) hablamos** | we speak |
| **(ellos) hablan** | they speak |
| **(ustedes) hablan** | you (all) speak |

**-er verb conjugation**

|  **Pronoun**  |  **Ending**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | -o |
| **tú** | -es |
| **él/ella** | -e | 
| **nosotros/nosotras** | -emos |
| **ellos/ellas** | -en |
| **ustedes** | -en |

Examples:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **comer**  | to eat |
| **(yo) como** | I eat |
| **(tú) comes** | you eat |
| **(él/ella) come** | he/she eats | 
| **(nosotros) comemos** | we eat |
| **(ellos) comen** | they eat |
| **(ustedes) comen** | you (all) eat |

**-ir verb conjugation**

|  **Pronoun**  |  **"-ir" Verb Endings**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | -o |
| **tú** | -es |
| **él/ella** | -e | 
| **nosotros** | -imos |
| **ellos** | -en |
| **ustedes** | -en |

Examples:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **escribir**  | to write |
| **(yo) escribo** | I write |
| **(tú) escribes** | you write |
| **(él/ella) escribe** | he/she writes | 
| **(nosotros) escribimos** | we write |
| **(ellos) escriben** | they write |
| **(ustedes) escriben** | you (all) write |

**Tener**

Tener (to have) is an irregular verb, so we just have to memorize its conjugation.

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **tener**  | to have |
| **(yo) tengo** | I have |
| **(tú) tienes** | you have |
| **(él/ella) tiene** | he/she has | 
| **(nosotros) tenemos** | we have |
| **(ellos) tienen** | they have |
| **(ustedes) tienen** | you (all) have |

title: Reflexive verbs
text:
The **reflexive** is when the *subject* performing an action and the *object* receiving that action are the same.

Where English has the -self pronouns (myself, yourself, etc.) for this kind of action, Spanish has its own set of **reflexive pronouns**:

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **me**  | myself |
| **te**  | yourself |
| **se**  | himself, herself, itself |
| **nos**  | ourselves |
| **se**  | themselves, yourselves |

When you're talking about parts of the body, use the definite article (el, la) rather than the possessive.

*For example: "Me cepillo **el** pelo" is **correct**. "Me cepillo **mi** pelo" is incorrect.*

**Options**

When there is more than one verb, you have two options: to include the pronoun ahead of the conjugated verb, or to place it at the end of the infinitive.

**Me quiero bañar.**
**Quiero bañarme.**
*I want to take a bath.*

**Ir**

There's one key verb here that doesn't really play by the rules of the reflexive, and that is **ir** (*to go*). Its reflexive form is **irse**, and it means *to leave*.

**Yo voy a la oficina.**
*I go to the office.*

**Me voy de la oficina.**
*I leave from the office.*

title: State of being
text:
**Pronouns**

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **yo**  | I/me |
| **tú**  | you |
| **usted**  | you (formal) |
| **él**  | he |
| **ella**  | she |
| **nosotros/nosotras**  | us |
| **ellos/ellas**  | them |
| **ustedes**  | you (all) |

Conjugation for **ser** (*to be*):

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **ser**  | to be |
| **(yo) soy** | I am |
| **(tú) eres** | you are |
| **(él/ella) es** | he/she is | 
| **(nosotros) somos** | we are |
| **(ellos) son** | they are |
| **(ustedes) son** | you (all) are |

**Masculine and feminine nouns**

In Spanish, every noun has a gender, meaning that it's either "masculine" or "feminine." Masculine nouns use the definite article "el" for singular and "los" for plural (el perro, los perros) and feminine nouns use "la" and "las" (la puerta, las puertas).

*Most* words that end in "-o" are masculine, and *most* words that end in "-a" are feminine, but the most reliable way to tell if a noun is masculine or feminine is to look at which **definite article** it uses: *"el"* or *"la."*

**Here are a few rules-of-thumb on nouns that don't follow this pattern.**

Here are a few of the most common "opposites" (masculine nouns ending in -a and feminine nouns ending in -o) that you'll encounter.

| *Spanish* | *English* |
| ---------- | ---------|
| el día | the day |
| el mapa | the map |
| el planeta | the planet |
| la mano | the hand |
| la radio | the radio |
| la foto | the photo |
| la moto | the motorbike |

Some nouns that refer to people have both a masculine and feminine form, depending on who they're referencing:

| *Masculine* | *Feminine* | *English* |
| ---------- | -------- | ---------|
| el doctor | la doctora | the doctor |
| el profesor | la profesora | the professor |
| el maestro | la maestra | the teacher |
| el arquitecto | la arquitecta | the architect |
| el cocinero | la cocinera | the chef |

Even though they end in an "-a," words that end in "-ma" specifically are almost always masculine.

| *Spanish* | *English* |
| ---------- | ---------|
| el idioma | the language |
| el programa | the program |
| el problema | the problem |
| el drama | the drama |
| el poema | the poem |
| el sistema | the system |

There are only a few notable exceptions to this rule:

| *Spanish* | *English* |
| ---------- | ---------|
| la pluma | the pen |
| la cama | the bed |
| la forma | the form |

All words that end in **-sión**, **-ción**, **-dad**, **-tad**, or **-tud** are feminine.

title: Subjunctive mood
text:
A *tense* lets us know when something is taking place (past, present, future, ongoing, etc.), while a *mood* expresses how the speaker feels about an action.

In contrast, the **subjunctive** mood is used for *subjectivity*, anything that's not certain or objective. This includes things like desires, doubts, opinions, and uncertainty.

To conjugation verbs in the subjunctive, we start with the **yo** form of the verb (the first-person present tense). Then, we drop the -o at the end to get the *stem* before adding the proper ending.

- hablar -> hablo -> habl- -> **hable**
- escribir -> escribo -> escrib- -> **escriba**

Thinking about it this way helps because it covers both regular and irregular verbs.

- comer -> como -> com- -> **coma**
- querer -> quiero -> quier- -> **quiera**

Here are the subjunctive endings:

|  **pronoun** |  **-ar**  |  **-er, -ir**  | 
| --------- | -------- | -------- |
| yo | **-e** | **-a** |
| tú | **-es** | **-as** |
| él/ella | **-e** | **-a** |
| nosotros | **-emos** | **-amos** |
| ellos | **-en** | **-an** |

Examples:

|  **hablar** |  **comer**  |  **escribir**  | 
| --------- | -------- | -------- |
| hable | coma | escriba |
| hables | comas | escribas |
| hable | coma | escriba |
| hablemos | comamos | escribamos |
| hablen | coman | escriban |
